title: About
text:
The djehuty community brings together users, contributors, developers, research data professionals, and everyone interested in the future of the djehuty platform.
Our goal is to create an open space for collaboration, knowledge sharing, and discussion around djehuty’s development and use. Through community meetings, discussions, proposals, and shared experiences, we work together to improve the platform and support the research data community.

title: About
text:
How we work together

Meet. Once a month we hold an open online Community Hour to discuss recent developments, upcoming work, and your topics. Dates are in the calendar.
Discuss. Ideas, questions and proposals live in the GitHub discussions.
Contribute. Whether you report an issue, improve documentation, or write code, there is a place for you. See ways to contribute.

title: Ways to contribute
text: Everyone is welcome, regardless of experience level or background. You don’t need to write code to make a difference: feedback, questions, documentation and testing all help djehuty grow.

title: Ways to contribute
text:
Join the conversation

Attend a Community Hour. Our monthly online meeting is open to everyone. Find out what to expect and check the calendar for the next date.
Take part in discussions. Ask questions, share ideas, or comment on proposals in the GitHub discussions.
Bring a topic. Want the community to discuss something? Add it to the agenda.

title: Ways to contribute
text:
Share feedback and report issues
Tell us about your experience with djehuty: what works well, what is confusing, and what is missing.

Report a bug or suggest a feature in the issue tracker. Please search existing issues first, and describe what you expected and what happened. Steps to reproduce help a lot.
See what is planned in the release roadmap, and tell us what matters most to you.

title: Ways to contribute
text:
Contribute code
Code contributions are welcome, from small fixes to new features. The full process is in CONTRIBUTING.md.






Important



Found a security vulnerability? Don’t open a public issue or PR — see SECURITY.md instead.

title: Ways to contribute
text:
Improve documentation, testing and design
Good documentation and careful testing are as valuable as code. You can:

read the documentation and tell us where it is unclear, outdated or missing,
test new releases and report what you find,
share ideas for a clearer, more accessible interface.

title: Ways to contribute
text:
Improve this website
This website is built with Quarto and lives in the community/ directory of the djehuty repository. To fix a typo, add a resource or write up meeting notes, use the Edit this page link on any page, or open an issue or pull request.

title: Ways to contribute
text:
Help the community grow

Share how your institution or project uses djehuty, for example in a Community Hour.
Invite colleagues who might benefit from the project or the community.
Welcome newcomers in discussions and meetings.

title: Community Hour
text:
The Community Hour is our monthly, open online meeting for the djehuty community. It is a relaxed space to:

hear about recent developments and upcoming work,
discuss community contributions and feature requests,
ask questions and share feedback and ideas,
meet other users, contributors and repository managers.

Everyone is welcome: users, contributors, developers, repository administrators, or simply the curious. You don’t need to be an expert or to speak; listening in is perfectly fine.

title: Community Hour
text:
When and how to join






NoteNext meeting



We meet every last Wednesday of the month, 3–4 PM Amsterdam time (CET/CEST), online on Google Meet: https://meet.google.com/zbt-mvxe-feq
Exact dates are in the calendar.



Add the next meeting to your calendar
Just want this one on your calendar? Use the Add to calendar button on the home page. It adds a single event straight into your normal calendar, the same as any other meeting invite — nothing separate to manage.


Subscribe to every Community Hour
Come regularly? Subscribe once and every future Community Hour appears automatically, including changes, with nothing to add by hand.






Note



A subscription always shows up as its own calendar (e.g. “djehuty Community Hour”) rather than merging into your main one. That’s how calendar subscriptions work, not something particular to this feed — it’s what lets your calendar app know to keep it updated.








TipHow to add the subscription






Apple Calendar, and most Google Calendars: Click Subscribe below — it should open your calendar app directly.
Outlook (web, new Outlook, or classic desktop): Click Copy link, then in Outlook go to Add calendar → Subscribe from web (classic desktop: Open Calendar → From Internet..), paste the link, and select Import/Subscribe.
Subscribe button doesn’t do anything in your browser?: click Copy link and paste it into your calendar app’s “subscribe by URL” option manually.

New meetings appear in this feed automatically as they’re scheduled — calendar apps typically re-check it about once a day.

title: Community Hour
text:
What to expect
A typical Community Hour follows this outline:

Welcome and short introductions
Project updates: recent releases and ongoing development
Community topics: items from the agenda, including contributions and feature requests
Open discussion and any other business
Wrap-up: summary of actions and the date of the next meeting

We follow the djehuty Code of Conduct in every meeting.

title: Community Hour
section: Add a point to the agenda
text:
Add a point to the agenda
Do you want the community to discuss something? Anyone can propose an agenda item.

Open an issue in the community repository, titled “Agenda: your topic”.
Briefly describe the topic, why it matters, and how much time you think you need.
Add links to related issues, discussions or documents.
Submit it before the meeting, ideally at least a few days ahead, so the organisers can plan the agenda.

Can’t attend live? Add your item anyway and say so in the description. We will discuss it and share the outcome in the meeting notes.

title: Community Hour
section: Add a point to the agenda
text:
Add a point to the agenda
Want the community to discuss something? Add it directly to the Rolling Notes document under the agenda for the next meeting — no approval needed, just add your topic in a line or two, ideally a few days before the meeting so there’s time to plan around it.
Can’t attend live? Add your item anyway and check the meeting notes afterwards for the outcome.
